The numbers are truly astounding (see additional tweet below more for more info!), and the vault represents an insanely exciting proof-of-concept in AI-run trading!

Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

Halloween is right around the corner, but job seekers have been ghosted all year. In fact, 86% of recent job seekers say they’ve encountered a posting that they suspected was not tied to an actual hiring need, according to a new Ghost Jobs Report by ResumeBuilder.com. Even worse, 58% say they’ve interviewed for a position they later suspected was a ghost job. When you need to find work, it’s tempting to copy, paste and apply to everything. Job seekers are sending out 30% more applications on LinkedIn than they did before the pandemic, LinkedIn CEO Dan Shapero told The Wall Street Journal last month. But when some of those job postings aren’t even real, more applications just mean more wasted time. So how do you avoid getting ghosted? Follow these steps before submitting your next application. Focus on quality over quantity. Be deliberate with your applications and search for job postings where you meet most of the requirements. Verify on the company website. If you can’t find the position on the company careers page, think twice before you spend time applying. Get in touch with a real person. Message a recruiter, someone on the team on LinkedIn or email them to confirm the role is active. Look for a referral you can trust. Get someone to vouch for your work ethic and boost your application if you feel confident the role is real. There’s no foolproof way to avoid ghost jobs, but there are steps you can take so they don’t consistently haunt your job search. — Colleen Batchelder, Contributor WORK SMARTER  Practical insights and advice from Forbes staff and contributors to help you succeed in your job, accelerate your career and lead smarter.
